content.value_statement: Starting a Convex app can require several framework-specific setup steps. This skill guides scaffolding, provider wiring, environment variables, and first validation checks.
actual_capabilities: Helps choose a Convex starter template for new projects.
Adds Convex to existing React, Next.js, Vue, Svelte, or similar apps.
Shows where to place ConvexProvider and ConvexReactClient in frontend roots.
Explains framework-specific Convex environment variable names.
Guides first Convex schema, query, mutation, and UI validation steps.
Separates interactive Convex dev commands from work an agent should run.
limitations: It does not provide a complete authentication implementation.
It expects the Convex CLI and npm tooling to be available.
It does not replace a production deployment or security review.
It gives starter patterns, not full application architecture.

use_cases.title: Prototype a New App
use_cases.description: Create a new frontend and Convex backend with a starter template and a clear first validation path.

use_cases.title: Add Backend to Frontend
use_cases.description: Install Convex in an existing app and wire the provider at the correct framework entry point.

use_cases.title: Configure Headless Development
use_cases.description: Use anonymous agent mode when browser login is unavailable in a cloud or headless environment.

prompt_templates.title: Create a New Convex App
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a fresh project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Set up a new Convex app for a simple React prototype. Choose the best starter template, explain the commands, and list what I should verify first.

prompt_templates.title: Add Convex to React
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate setup for an existing frontend.
prompt_templates.prompt: Add Convex to this existing React app. Identify the app entry point, install the package, wire the provider, and tell me how to confirm the client connects.

prompt_templates.title: Configure Next.js App Router
prompt_templates.prompt: Configure Convex for this Next.js App Router project. Add the client provider, place it in the root layout, and use the correct public environment variable.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Dev and Production Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Convex setup for development and production readiness. Separate dev watcher steps, agent mode needs, deployment timing, and first schema validation.

output_examples.input: Set up Convex for a new React app.
output_examples.output: The assistant selects a React starter template, prepares the scaffold steps, asks the user to run the Convex dev loop, and lists verification checks.

output_examples.input: Add Convex to my existing Next.js project.
output_examples.output: The assistant identifies the App Router provider location, explains the public Convex URL variable, and verifies that generated types are available.

output_examples.input: Use Convex from a cloud coding agent.
output_examples.output: The assistant chooses anonymous agent mode, explains why browser login is unavailable, and keeps the development watcher separate from normal code edits.

best_practices: Ask the user to run long-running Convex dev watchers in their own terminal.
Create Convex clients at module scope so frontend renders do not recreate them.
Verify generated Convex types before building queries, mutations, or UI components.
anti_patterns: Do not run production deployment commands during normal development setup.
Do not create Convex clients inside React component render functions.
Do not assume every framework uses the same Convex environment variable name.

faq.question: What does this skill set up?
faq.answer: It helps create a Convex project or add Convex to an existing frontend app.

faq.question: Can it work with an existing app?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers installing Convex, wiring the provider, and setting the correct environment variable.

faq.question: Does it run Convex dev automatically?
faq.answer: Usually no. It tells the user to run long-running interactive commands in their own terminal.

faq.question: Which frameworks are covered?
faq.answer: It includes React, Vite, Next.js, Vue, Svelte, React Native, Remix, and related quickstart paths.

faq.question: Does it configure authentication?
faq.answer: It can choose auth starter templates, but full authentication setup belongs in a separate skill.

faq.question: Does it cover production deployment?
faq.answer: It explains when to deploy, but it does not perform a complete release checklist.
